an4.11:1.1: (1) “Bhikkhus, if a sensual thought, a thought of ill will, or a thought of harming arises in a bhikkhu while walking,
an4.11:1.2: and he tolerates it, does not abandon it, dispel it, terminate it, and obliterate it,
an4.11:1.3: then that bhikkhu is said to be devoid of ardor and moral dread; he is constantly and continuously lazy and lacking in energy while walking.
an4.11:2.1: (2) “If a sensual thought … arises in a bhikkhu while standing … (3) If a sensual thought … arises in a bhikkhu while sitting … (4) If a sensual thought, a thought of ill will,
an4.11:4.1: or a thought of harming arises in a bhikkhu while wakefully lying down,
an4.11:4.2: and he tolerates it, does not abandon it, dispel it, terminate it, and obliterate it,
an4.11:4.3: then that bhikkhu is said to be devoid of ardor and moral dread; he is constantly and continuously lazy and lacking in energy while wakefully lying down.
an4.11:5.1: (1) “But, bhikkhus, if a sensual thought, a thought of ill will, or a thought of harming arises in a bhikkhu while walking,
an4.11:5.2: and he does not tolerate it but abandons it, dispels it, terminates it, and obliterates it,
an4.11:5.3: then that bhikkhu is said to be ardent and to dread wrongdoing; he is constantly and continuously energetic and resolute while walking.
an4.11:6.1: (2) “If a sensual thought … arises in a bhikkhu while standing … (3) If a sensual thought … arises in a bhikkhu while sitting … (4) If a sensual thought, a thought of ill will,
an4.11:8.1: or a thought of harming arises in a bhikkhu while wakefully lying down,
an4.11:8.2: and he does not tolerate it but abandons it, dispels it, terminates it, and obliterates it,
an4.11:8.3: then that bhikkhu is said to be ardent and to dread wrongdoing; he is constantly and continuously energetic and resolute while walking.”
